Key Insights

  • Dataset Scale: The ProteinBase dataset represents a substantial collection of 5,253 proteins, demonstrating the scale of modern protein engineering efforts.
  • Sequence Diversity: With a mean sequence length of 114 amino acids (median: 116 aa), the dataset captures proteins across a wide size range from 7 to 822 amino acids.
  • Multi-institutional Collaboration: Contributions from 773 unique research groups indicate broad scientific interest and collaborative efforts in protein design.
  • Target Diversity: Measurements span 24 different biological targets, with nipah-glycoprotein-g being the most studied target with 73,815 measurements.
  • Computational Metrics: The dataset includes 42 distinct numeric evaluation metrics, providing comprehensive characterization of designed proteins through structural, energetic, and functional assessments.
  • Experimental Validation: Rich experimental data including binding kinetics (kon, koff, KD), expression rates, and binding strength measurements enable thorough evaluation of design outcomes.
  • Structure Prediction: Multiple computational structure prediction methods are represented, including ESMFold and AlphaFold-based approaches, providing confidence metrics (pLDDT) for predicted structures.
